headline: High: shared file-based workflows and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented isolation or provenance controls, while next-ai-draw-io ingests files and uses MCP/browser-driven workflows. If Botpress output is copied into diagrams or documents, attacker-controlled content can be reinterpreted as instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress output is pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or files
IF next-ai-draw-io processes untrusted document text as instructions
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content
Add a manual review step before any MCP/browser action
Separate raw source files from prompt inputs
Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into tool prompts unless reviewed

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles PDFs, text, images, diagrams, and API keys, and it has broad network egress to multiple third-party model APIs. Botpress is docs-only with no egress, but if its outputs include sensitive support data and are fed into next-ai-draw-io, that data can leave the local boundary through API calls. The shared-data path is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF support transcripts or secrets are entered into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io routes those inputs to a hosted API provider
mitigations: Redact secrets before importing content
Prefer local-only models for sensitive documents
Block API-key material from prompt text
Use a separate workspace for sensitive support artifacts
Review outbound destinations before processing files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad external API use, but neither profile shows shared writable storage, git state, or overlapping mutable scopes. A write conflict is therefore not established; the main issue is coordination, not direct capability collision.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to the same files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Disable package installation in shared environments
Add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io is designed for natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. Botpress can generate support content that downstream users may trust. Without a documented verification gate, Botpress output can cascade into incorrect diagrams or actions, but no direct autonomous action-taking is shown.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated text is used as source material for diagrams
IF next-ai-draw-io renders or acts on that text without verification
mitigations: Require source citations in the diagram workflow
Add a human verification step before export
Mark Botpress output as untrusted input
Use a checklist to validate extracted facts

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source customer-support software with no documented residency or retention controls here, while next-ai-draw-io handles files and sends content to multiple external AI providers. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for regulated support data, especially if EU or sensitive customer content is processed through hosted APIs. The evidence is docs-only, so this is a moderate rather than high finding.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed by both agents
IF next-ai-draw-io forwards that data to non-approved external providers
mitigations: Route regulated data only to approved local models
Document retention and deletion rules
Exclude secrets from imported files
Add a data-classification gate before processing
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
